name: Option 1: Metso Superior MKII 60-89
description: Primary crusher upgrade to increase capacity from 4000 to 5000 tph with 8-inch product size

assumptions: Assumes standard site conditions (no extreme terrain)
Includes foundation but excludes major earthworks
Based on vendor quote from Metso dated 2023-08-15
Lang factors from Richardson 2019 study
CEPCI escalation from 2020 (596.2) to 2025 (est. 763.0)

downstream_impacts.rationale: Coarser primary crusher product (8 inches vs 6 inches) reduces secondary crushing load. Existing equipment can handle reduced duty with lower power consumption and wear.
assumptions: Secondary crushers currently operating at 95% capacity
Power consumption scales linearly with load
Liner life increases by 20% with reduced load

downstream_impacts.rationale: Coarser feed to SAG mill (8 inches vs 6 inches) increases grinding work required. Mill currently at 88% capacity; upgrade to larger motor and additional ball charge required to maintain throughput.
assumptions: SAG mill work index increases 12% with coarser feed
Motor upgrade from 15MW to 17MW required
Ball charge increase from 12% to 14% filling
Additional power cost at $0.08/kWh

downstream_impacts.rationale: Throughput increase from 4000 to 5000 tph exceeds existing conveyor capacity (4200 tph). Belt width upgrade from 1400mm to 1600mm required.
assumptions: Existing belt operating at 95% of rated capacity
Belt upgrade can reuse existing structure and drives
Includes new belt purchase and installation labor

downstream_impacts.rationale: Existing ore stockpile has 30,000 tonne capacity with 6-hour surge capacity at new throughput. No modification required.
assumptions: Stockpile reclaim rate can be increased to match new throughput
Power rate of $0.08/kWh based on site contract
Operating 8000 hours per year at 1120 kW
Maintenance at 2.87% of installed cost per Richardson guidelines
Labor: 1 operator per shift, 4 shifts, $20k per operator
Consumables: Liners replaced every 4000 hours at $500k per set

validation_warnings: SAG mill capacity margin reduced to 7% - below recommended 15% minimum
Payback period of 8.4 years exceeds typical 5-year corporate hurdle
Downstream CAPEX delta adds 21% to base equipment cost
rationale: Best balance of capacity increase and total cost. Higher upfront CAPEX offset by significant OPEX savings in secondary crushing. SAG mill capacity concern can be mitigated with optimized operating parameters.
